# Chapter 13: The Unwritten Future

What Bob knew, at seventy-two, was this: he had lived fully. That was not a boast or a summary; it was a simple accounting. He had loved and lost and loved again. He had built things that worked and things that failed. He had been present for the birth of his children and the survival of his daughter and the arrival of grandchildren who looked at him with the uncomplicated trust that only the very young can offer.
